document.title: Deposition of Raymond T. Holloway (excerpt)
document.case: Vance v. Meridian Logistics, Inc., No. 24-CV-00912
document.note: Synthetic sample input for the CrossExam deterministic fallback parser. Only the demo-relevant pages of an otherwise 912-page deposition are included. Page 147 contains the key admission about the warehouse on the night of the 14th; page 488 contains a direct contradiction of that testimony.

lines: Q. Mr. Holloway, where were you on the night of the 14th?
A. I was at the warehouse on the night of the 14th, working the late shift.
Q. The Meridian distribution warehouse on Industrial Parkway?
A. Yes. That warehouse. I clocked in a little before ten and stayed until close.
Q. Let me take you back to the evening of the 14th. Were you anywhere near the warehouse?
A. No. I never went to the warehouse that night. I was home the entire evening of the 14th.
Q. So you were not at the Industrial Parkway facility at all?
A. Correct. I did not set foot in that building on the 14th.
Q. Who else had keys to the loading dock?
A. Just me and the shift supervisor, Dana Wexler, as far as I know.
Q. And the security logs would reflect badge entries for that dock?
A. They should, yes. Every entry gets logged by badge number.
